bandReport.notes:
COVERAGE. 21 items, 44-64, no gaps. Printed page numbers on my five pages read 23, 25, 27, 29, 31 - consecutive odd numbers - so no English page falls between them and the even printed pages are the Hindi side. Every page carried items; no page key is empty. p20 (printed 21, previous band) ends with item 43's options and p32 (printed 33, next band) opens item 65, so both my boundaries are clean: firstComplete and lastComplete are both true.

DECIMAL SEPARATOR: RAISED MIDDLE DOT (U+00B7). Passage-2 (item 50) prints 'another 1·5 lakh'. Verified at 5x against the baseline full stop in 'greatest risk.' two lines above - the glyph sits at mid x-height, not on the baseline. Preserved as U+00B7, matching the shipped sibling Paper II files (2022-p2, 2023-p2 and 2025-p2 all preserve it). It is the ONLY decimal number in my band.

CROSS-BAND SHARED CONTEXT - NEEDS A HUMAN EYE AT MERGE. Items 44-48 are the tail of a SIX-item block (43-48) whose governing information is printed on p20-c2, a page belonging to the PREVIOUS band. Item 43 is on that page; items 44-48 are mine. I opened p20 and transcribed the setup into `context` for all five of my items, byte-identical across them. But band b will transcribe the SAME setup for item 43, and if our two copies differ by so much as one glyph the block silently splits into two rendering groups and passes every gate. The two places ours are most likely to disagree: (i) 'Further, it is given that—' ends in an EM DASH (U+2014), verified at 2.6x zoom off p20-c2; (ii) the five sub-clauses are printed as an indented (i)-(v) list with NO terminating punctuation on any of them, and I have kept them on their own lines with none added. Please diff item 43's context against items 44-48's before commit.

PASSAGE STRUCTURE. p22-c2 opens 'Directions for the following 8 (eight) items :' / 'Read the following eight passages and answer the items that follow. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.' It is EIGHT passages over EIGHT items, so the mapping is strictly ONE passage to ONE item - Passage-1 governs item 49, Passage-2 item 50, and so on to Passage-8 and item 56. None of these eight is shared. Each passage is still placed in that item's `context`, following the shipped convention rather than the brief's rule-of-thumb: I checked all six shipped sibling Paper II files and every one of them puts a single-item passage in `context` (1-item context groups number 23 in 2023-p2, 18 in 2019-p2, 15 in 2020-p2, 9 in 2024-p2), and 2020-p2's own band notes call the resulting lonely-context warning 'legitimate'. No hash collision results: each of these eight stems carries its own distinguishing text or its own option set. Per the same shipped convention I have NOT put the 'Directions for the following N items :' header or the 'Passage-N' label into `context` - zero shipped p2 items contain either string.

The only genuinely SHARED context in my band is the graph block governing items 63 and 64.

TWO PAIRS OF BYTE-IDENTICAL STEMS, both safe but both worth knowing about. Items 51 and 52 both read 'Which one of the following is the most important implication of the passage?' and items 46 and 48 both read 'Which one of the following statements is correct?'. In each pair the option sets are completely different, so the four content hashes stay distinct - this is exactly the pattern the brief warns about and exactly the shape 2019-p2 items 79/80 shipped in, so it is precedented, not new.

FIGURES. Four items are unanswerable from text alone - 61 (progress line graph), 62 (three-block stand), and 63/64 (birthrate/death rate line graph). Each carries a `[FIGURE: ...]` marker inline at the point the booklet prints the figure and is flagged `figure-required`, following the convention band b-a of this same paper already established at items 1 and 5. The descriptions are deliberately geometric - axis labels, tick values, curve shapes and crossing points as drawn - and stop short of stating any conclusion the item asks the candidate to draw.

PUNCTUATION AS PRINTED. This booklet puts a SPACE before a colon ('Consider the sequence given below :') but NO space before a question mark ('What is the next term of the series?'). Both are reproduced as printed. Apostrophes are written as the ASCII straight quote throughout, matching the dominant shipped convention (402 straight against 65 curly across the six shipped p2 merged files); the booklet itself sets them curly.

PRINTED DEFECT, TRANSCRIBED UNCORRECTED: Passage-1 (item 49) reads 'treat climate change as real threat' - the indefinite article before 'real threat' is missing. Flagged on the item, not corrected.

COLUMN CROPS. All ten crops were usable and every item was read from the column images, never from the whole page. Each -c2 crop carries a narrow strip of the neighbouring column's right-hand edge down its left margin (isolated fragments such as 'is', 'in', 'of'); these are cosmetic, belong to the c1 text I had already read in full, and cost nothing. Two passages span the gutter and were joined by reading c1 to its end and then c2 from its top: Passage-3 on p24 ('... Science, whatever' | 'unpleasant consequences it may have ...') and Passage-6 on p26 ('... the environment today is very' | 'different. It is a complex, volatile ...'). Both gutter breaks were located on the whole-page image first, then both halves read off the column crops.

SCAN ARTEFACT: on p30 the item numbers 61, 62, 63 and 64 are printed white-on-a-dark-block rather than in the plain bold used everywhere else in the booklet. The digits are unambiguous at zoom. It affects nothing but is noted in case a later reader meets it on this page.

questions.stem:
Consider the following graph :
[FIGURE: a line graph. The vertical axis is labelled '% of work' and is marked 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%. The horizontal axis carries six labelled vertical gridlines reading, left to right, '1st April', 'May', 'June', 'July', 'Aug' and '1st Sept'. Two curves both start together at 0% on the 1st April gridline. A DASHED curve, labelled 'Expected progress' by an arrow, rises steeply at first and then flattens - passing roughly 28% at May, 50% at June, 60% at July and 70% at Aug - before rising again to reach 100% at the 1st Sept gridline. A SOLID line, labelled 'Actual progress' by an arrow, rises far more gently and almost straight - passing roughly 12% at May, 22% at June, 32% at July and 43% at Aug - and then turns sharply upward, crossing the dashed curve between Aug and 1st Sept and reaching the 100% line just short of the 1st Sept gridline.]
Which one of the following statements is not correct with reference to the graph given above?

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: The work was actually completed before the expected time.

options.label: D
options.text: During the period from 1st April to 1st September, at no time was the actual progress more than the expected progress.

questions.context:
Consider the following graph in which the birthrate and death rate of a country are given, and answer the two items that follow.
[FIGURE: a line graph on a ruled grid. The vertical axis is labelled 'Birth and death rates per thousand' and is marked 0, 10, 20 and 30 with minor ticks between. The horizontal axis is labelled 'Years' and is marked 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000 and 2010 with minor ticks between. A SOLID curve labelled 'Birthrate' begins at 30 in 1970, holds nearly level for the first few years, then falls through the 1980s and 1990s, easing off to about 18 around 2000 and running almost flat at roughly 18 to 2010. A DASHED curve labelled 'Death rate' begins at about 25 in 1970 and falls steadily and more steeply throughout, flattening to about 7 around 2000 and running almost flat at roughly 7 to 2010. The two curves do not meet at any point.]
